title: The search that leaked filters
blurb: Raw filters hit fields outside the allowlist and caches ignored filters.
prompt: A crafted filter string surfaced unpublished products, and a cached unfiltered result set was served to a filtered query. The model-generated draft interpolates filter text into the engine query and caches by raw query string. Review it, fix it, and prove filters are allowlisted and cache keys are complete.
aiNote: The draft passes caller filter syntax through to the query engine, so fields outside the per-tenant allowlist are addressable, and its cache key omits filters, tenant and index version, so one result set answers queries it never matched.
testIdea: Send a filter naming a forbidden field and assert 400; cache an unfiltered query then run the filtered version and assert a miss; force a shard timeout and assert partial is marked and duplicates are deduped.
followUps: What belongs in a query cache key versus a cache eviction signal?
How would you rank results so a partial merge stays stable?
When is serving a stale price acceptable?
